title: Braided Greek Tsoureki
summary: A glossy, braided Greek sweet bread fragranced with orange zest and warm mahleb spice, with a soft, pull-apart crumb.
equipment: 2 baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: optional; from Middle Eastern or Greek shops
optional; grind with 1 tsp of the sugar

ingredients.item: large egg, beaten with 1 tbsp milk

steps.title: Make and rise the dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, mahleb, mastic and orange zest, then add the milk, eggs and alcohol-free vanilla extract and knead for 5 minutes. Add the butter in pieces and knead for a further 8-10 minutes, until the dough turns silky and elastic and stretches into long, stringy threads when pulled. Cover and leave to rise for 2-3 hours, until doubled - this rich, buttery dough takes its time, so don't rush it.

steps.title: Braid and prove
steps.text: Halve the dough and divide each half into 3 pieces. Roll each piece into a 45cm rope, pinch three ropes together at one end, braid them loosely and tuck the ends underneath. Set the braids on the trays, cover and prove for 1-1½ hours until puffy and visibly larger.

steps.title: Bake to a deep shine
steps.text: At 170°C (150°C fan), brush the braids with egg wash twice for a deep shine, and bake for 30-35 minutes, covering with foil after 20 minutes if they're browning too fast. The tsoureki is done once it's a deep mahogany colour and the centre reads 88-90°C, which keeps this enriched dough soft rather than dry.

steps.title: Cool before slicing
steps.text: At least 1 hour on the wire rack is needed before slicing, so the soft, stringy crumb has time to firm up enough to hold a clean cut.

tips: Knead the enriched dough until it's properly elastic and stringy - stopping too early leaves tsoureki dense instead of soft and pull-apart.
Don't rush the first rise; this buttery, egg-rich dough is naturally slower than a plain loaf.
Double-brush with egg wash for the deep, glossy shine tsoureki is known for.
Cover with foil if the braid is browning before the centre reaches temperature, so the crust doesn't turn bitter.
Let the loaf cool fully before cutting, or the soft crumb will tear rather than slice cleanly.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Warm briefly in a low oven before serving if you'd like it piping hot again. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
